```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r}
library(pdecompR)
```

The mesh is the foundation of every finite-element computation. pdecompR
represents two-dimensional triangular meshes with explicit topology and
named boundary regions, and it validates every mesh it builds.

## Domains

A domain is a pure geometric description. Rectangles have four named sides;
polygons name each side individually.

```{r}
pde_domain("rectangle", x = c(0, 2), y = c(0, 1))

L <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(2, 0), c(2, 1), c(1, 1), c(1, 2), c(0, 2))
dom <- pde_domain("polygon", vertices = L,
                  markers = c("bottom", "right", "step", "step", "top", "left"))
dom
```

Validation rejects degenerate geometry: repeated vertices, zero-length
sides, zero area and self-intersecting boundaries. Clockwise polygons are
reordered (their markers follow) and a message says so.

```{r, error = TRUE}
pde_domain("polygon", vertices = rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 1), c(1, 0), c(0, 1)))
```

## Structured meshes

`pde_mesh_rectangle()` generates structured meshes with three diagonal
patterns. Corner nodes belong to both adjacent sides.

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 2.6}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
for (p in c("right", "left", "alternating")) {
  plot(pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 4, pattern = p), main = p, markers = FALSE)
}
par(op)
```

## The mesh object

A `pde_mesh` stores

* `nodes`: an $n \times 2$ matrix of coordinates;
* `triangles`: an $m \times 3$ integer matrix, counterclockwise;
* `edges`: the unique edges, and `element_edges` mapping each triangle's local
  edges $(v_1, v_2)$, $(v_2, v_3)$, $(v_3, v_1)$ to global edges;
* `edge_elements`: the one or two triangles sharing each edge;
* `boundary`: a data frame of boundary edges with nodes `n1`, `n2` (oriented
  with the domain on the left), the global edge, the parent element, the
  local edge and the marker.

```{r}
mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 2)
head(mesh$triangles)
mesh$boundary
```

## Validation

`pde_mesh()` builds a mesh from raw coordinates and connectivity and checks
it thoroughly. It rejects invalid node indices, repeated nodes in an element,
duplicate elements, zero-area triangles, unused nodes, edges shared by more
than two triangles, neighboring elements that overlap across a shared edge,
boundary definitions that do
not match the topological boundary, and elements that overlap without
sharing an edge. The last check uses two facts about a valid triangulation:
the corner angles around an interior node sum to $2\pi$ (at most $2\pi$ at
a boundary node), and boundary edges without a common node never touch.
Clockwise elements are an error unless reorientation is requested
explicitly.

```{r, error = TRUE}
P <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(1, 1), c(0, 1))
pde_mesh(P, rbind(c(1, 3, 2), c(1, 3, 4)))
m <- pde_mesh(P, rbind(c(1, 3, 2), c(1, 3, 4)), fix_orientation = TRUE)
m$info$reoriented
pde_mesh(rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(2, 0)), rbind(c(1, 2, 3)))
# two squares with their own nodes, overlapping in a quarter
P2 <- rbind(P, P + 0.5)
pde_mesh(P2, rbind(c(1, 2, 3), c(1, 3, 4), c(5, 6, 7), c(5, 7, 8)))
```

Boundary markers can be supplied as an explicit list of boundary edges; every
topological boundary edge must appear exactly once.

```{r}
be <- rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(3, 4), c(4, 1))
m <- pde_mesh(P, rbind(c(1, 2, 3), c(1, 3, 4)), be, c("inflow", "wall", "outflow", "wall"))
table(m$boundary$marker)
```

## Geometry and quality

`mesh_quality()` returns, per element, the area, longest and shortest edges,
minimum and maximum angles and the shape ratio $2r/R$ (inradius over
circumradius; 1 for equilateral triangles).

```{r}
summary(pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8))
head(mesh_quality(pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8)))
```

## Polygonal domains

`pde_mesh_polygon()` triangulates a simple polygon by ear clipping, flips
edges until the coarse triangulation is Delaunay, and refines uniformly until
the longest edge is at most `h`. Side markers are kept.

```{r}
mL <- pde_mesh_polygon(dom, h = 0.25)
summary(mL)
plot(mL, main = "L-shaped domain")
```

Polygons may have holes. Each hole is a simple polygon strictly inside the
outer one, and its sides get their own marker (`"hole"` by default). The
mesher connects every hole to the outer boundary by a bridge segment and
triangulates the resulting single polygon, so no external mesher is needed.

```{r}
sq <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(2, 0), c(2, 1), c(0, 1))
holes <- list(rbind(c(0.3, 0.3), c(0.7, 0.3), c(0.7, 0.7), c(0.3, 0.7)),
              cbind(1.4 + 0.25 * cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 13)[-13]),
                    0.5 + 0.25 * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 13)[-13])))
dh <- pde_domain("polygon", vertices = sq, holes = holes, hole_markers = c("square", "circle"))
mh <- pde_mesh_polygon(dh, h = 0.1)
table(mh$boundary$marker)
plot(mh, main = "Domain with two holes")
```

Holes that leave the outer polygon, overlap each other or touch a boundary
are rejected when the domain is created.

This mesher has no external dependencies but does not guarantee element
quality for arbitrary polygons. For complex geometry, generate a mesh with
[Gmsh](https://gmsh.info) and read it with `read_gmsh()`; physical line
groups become boundary markers.

```{r}
f <- system.file("extdata", "square.msh", package = "pdecompR")
gm <- read_gmsh(f)
table(gm$boundary$marker)
```

`write_vtk()` exports meshes and solutions to the VTK format for ParaView:
the legacy format by default, the XML `.vtu` format when the file name ends
in `.vtu` (raw binary by default, exact to the last bit; `format = "ascii"`
for text). `write_pvd()` writes a time-dependent solution as one `.vtu`
file per output time plus a `.pvd` collection that ParaView opens as an
animation.

## Refinement

`refine_uniform()` splits each triangle into four similar triangles.
`refine_mesh()` refines selected elements by newest vertex bisection and
keeps the mesh conforming: no hanging nodes appear, and the minimum angle
stays bounded.

```{r}
m <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 4)
for (k in 1:5) {
  P <- m$nodes; T <- m$triangles
  cx <- (P[T[, 1], 1] + P[T[, 2], 1] + P[T[, 3], 1]) / 3
  cy <- (P[T[, 1], 2] + P[T[, 2], 2] + P[T[, 3], 2]) / 3
  m <- refine_mesh(m, which(sqrt((cx - 0.5)^2 + (cy - 0.5)^2) < 0.15))
}
plot(m, main = "Local refinement around (0.5, 0.5)")
min(mesh_quality(m)$min_angle)
```

`transfer_function()` moves a function to another mesh by evaluating it at
the new degrees of freedom. Refined meshes are nested in their parents, so
P1 and P2 functions transfer exactly from coarse to fine meshes. Refined
meshes also record the parent edge of every new node in `info$new_nodes`.

## Selecting boundary parts

`boundary_nodes()` and `boundary_dofs()` select nodes by marker. For imported
meshes without physical groups, `set_boundary_marker()` relabels boundary
edges whose midpoints satisfy a predicate.

```{r}
m <- set_boundary_marker(pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8), "inlet",
                         function(x, y) x < 1e-12 & y > 0.25 & y < 0.75)
table(m$boundary$marker)
```
